answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with onyx-hard identity bonds: each agent locks a deposit and a verifiable work history before it can transact, so spawning a thousand fake identities in a meadow of sock puppets costs a thousand deposits. A new identity starts near zero trust and only earns weight slowly through successful attested work, while a comet-like burst of brand-new accounts gets rate-limited and quarantined until peers verify them. Attackers pay real capital per identity and gain nothing fast.
